terms.grammar: adverb with the preposition ad and the accusative
evidence: Cic. Amic. 33: ūsque ad extrēmum vītae diem
terms.comment: For “until he came”, a clause with dum or dōnec.
ad vesperum, until evening; ad multam noctem, until late at night.

phrases.latin: quamquam ille quidem nihil difficilius esse dīcēbat quam amīcitiam ūsque ad extrēmum vītae diem permanēre
phrases.english: though he used to say that nothing was harder than for a friendship to last until one’s dying day

phrases.latin: quae puerōs nōn didicisse turpe est, ea putant ūsque ad senectūtem esse discenda
phrases.english: they think that what it is a shame for boys not to have learned must be studied until old age

phrases.latin: convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus
phrases.english: every day I fill my table with neighbours, and with talk of every kind we keep the party going as far as we can, until late at night

phrases.latin: epistulam cum ā tē avidē exspectārem ad vesperum, ut soleō, ecce tibi nūntius puerōs vēnisse Rōmā!
phrases.english: as I was eagerly waiting until evening for a letter from you, as I always do, look, word comes that the boys have arrived from Rome!

phrases.latin: quis est tam stultus, quamvīs sit adulēscēns, cui sit explōrātum sē ad vesperum esse vīctūrum?
phrases.english: who is so foolish, however young, as to be sure he will live until evening?

phrases.latin: hāc contrōversiā ūsque ad noctem ductā senātus dīmissus est
phrases.english: this dispute dragged on until nightfall, and the senate was dismissed

usque.html: De Vaan s.v. usque: the length is uncertain and Romance continues both; he takes shortening as likelier than lengthening, which speaks for the long vowel. The lexicon has both spellings so far.
